    24→## 1. Contest Overview and Objectives
    25→
    26→### 1.1 Context
    27→
    28→The IEEE GRSS 2026 Data Fusion Contest (DFC26) provides a **Capella Space commercial SAR stack**: ~1582 unique collects, enabling 17,000+ possible interferometric pairs across multiple AOIs, with substantial diversity in mode, incidence angle, look direction, and orbital geometry.

    38→### 1.2 Contest Objectives (maps to evaluation criteria)

    40→| ID | Objective |
    41→|----|-----------|
    42→| O1 | Increase stack usability under geometry diversity by improving interferogram quality and unwrapping reliability (closure + unwrap metrics) |

    44→| O3 | Produce interpretable "temporal storytelling" artifacts: pair graphs, maps, timelines showing why the method helps |

    60→## 2. Dataset: Capella Space SAR Open Data
    61→
    62→### 2.1 Data Access
    63→
    64→```bash
    65→# Validate open access (no authentication required)
    66→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request s3://capella-open-data/data/
    67→
    68→# Inventory dataset size
    69→aws s3 ls --no-sign-request --recursive --summarize s3://capella-open-data/data/ > s3_inventory.txt
    70→```
    71→
    72→- **S3 bucket**: `s3://capella-open-data/data/` (region: `us-west-2`)
    73→- **STAC root**: `https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/catalog.json`
    74→- **Contest collection**: child link `"IEEE Data Contest 2026"` → `capella-open-data-ieee-data-contest/collection.json`
    75→- The catalog is **static STAC** (JSON files linked via root/child/item), NOT a STAC API — use `pystac`, not `pystac-client` unless building a local index.
    76→
    77→### 2.2 Product Format (Capella SLC)
    78→
    79→- **Format**: Cloud-Optimized GeoTIFF (`.tif`) + STAC JSON + extended JSON sidecar
    80→- **Pixel type**: Complex CInt16 (real Int16 + imaginary Int16 = 32 bits/pixel)
    81→- **Radiometric convention**: SLC relates to Beta Nought; a `scale_factor` in extended metadata converts to radar brightness
    82→- **Metadata parsing**: use `capella-reader` which provides orbit, Doppler, and ISCE3 adapter
    83→
    84→```python
    85→from capella_reader import CapellaSLC
    86→slc = CapellaSLC.from_file("path/to/slc.tif")
    87→orbit = slc.adapted.isce3_orbit  # ISCE3 orbit object
    88→```
    89→
    90→### 2.3 Compute/Storage Tiers
    91→
    92→| Tier | SLC count | Pair count | Storage | GPUs |
    93→|------|-----------|------------|---------|------|
    94→| Minimal (proof-of-pipeline) | 40–120 | 300–1500 | 1–3 TB | 1×24 GB |
    95→| Competitive (3–6 AOIs, multi-mode) | 200–600 | 3k–15k | 6–20 TB | 2×48 GB |
    96→| Ideal (many AOIs/modes) | 800–1582 | 10k–30k | 20–60 TB | 4–8×80 GB |
    97→
    98→**Target**: Competitive tier minimum to claim cross-geometry generalization.
    99→
   100→### 2.4 Required Additional Packages
   101→
   102→Beyond `requirements.txt`:
   103→```bash
   104→pip install boto3 pystac capella-reader dask geopandas
   105→# ISCE3 via conda-forge or from source
   106→conda install -c conda-forge isce3
   107→```
   108→
   109→---
   110→
   111→## 3. Success Metrics (Official)
   112→
   113→All five metrics must be implemented in `src/evaluation/` and reported per-AOI and aggregated.
   114→
   115→### 3.1 Triplet Closure Error
   116→
   117→**Definition**: For three acquisitions (i, j, k): `c_ijk(p) = wrap(φ_ij(p) + φ_jk(p) − φ_ik(p))`
   118→
   119→Aggregate as `median_p(|c_ijk(p)|)` then median over triplets.
   120→
   121→**Target**: Median closure error ↓ **30–50%** on stable pixels across multiple AOIs/modes.
   122→
   123→```python
   124→# src/evaluation/closure_metrics.py
   125→def triplet_closure_error(phi_ij, phi_jk, phi_ik):
   126→    """Returns per-pixel closure; report median and quantiles."""
   127→    closure = np.angle(np.exp(1j * (phi_ij + phi_jk - phi_ik)))
   128→    return closure
   129→```
   130→
   131→### 3.2 Unwrap Success Rate
   132→
   133→**Definition**: Pass/fail per interferogram:
   134→1. Unwrapped connected component covers ≥90% of stable mask
   135→2. Triplet closure gate: 95th percentile < 1 rad for triplets containing that edge
   136→
   137→**Baseline**: SNAPHU (statistical-cost network-flow MAP)
   138→
   139→**Target**: Unwrap success rate ↑ **+15–25 percentage points**.
   140→
   141→### 3.3 Percent Usable Pairs
   142→
   143→**Definition**: % of candidate edges passing ALL gates:
   144→- Median coherence > 0.35
   145→- Unwrap success
   146→- Closure gate
   147→
   148→**Target**: Percent usable pairs ↑ **+20–40%**.
   149→
   150→### 3.4 DEM NMAD
   151→
   152→**Definition**: `NMAD = 1.4826 × median(|e − median(e)|)` where `e = h_pred − h_ref`
   153→
   154→Computed on stable terrain mask; external reference DEM used **only for evaluation**, never as a training target.
   155→
   156→**Target**: DEM NMAD ↓ **15–25%** (where baseline geometry allows DEM sensitivity).
   157→
   158→### 3.5 Temporal Consistency Residual
   159→
   160→**Definition**: Stack inversion residual — solve `Ax ≈ φ` (SBAS-like); compute `‖W(Ax − φ)‖₂` or per-edge residual quantiles.
   161→
   162→**Target**: Temporal consistency residual ↓ **≥20%**.
   163→
   164→### 3.6 Recommended Evaluation Thresholds (Targets)
   165→
   166→| Metric | Target improvement |
   167→|--------|-------------------|
   168→| Closure error median | ↓ ≥30% |
   169→| Unwrap success rate | ↑ ≥15 pp |
   170→| Usable pairs | ↑ ≥25% |
   171→| Temporal residual | ↓ ≥20% |
   172→| DEM NMAD | ↓ ≥15% |
   173→

   176→## 4. Pipeline Architecture
   177→
   178→```
   179→S3 (Capella SAR) → STAC crawl → metadata parquet
   180→        |
   181→        v
   182→   Pair-graph construction (nodes=collects, edges=candidate pairs)
   183→   Edge scoring: Q_ij = f(Δt, Δθ_inc, Δθ_graze, B_perp, SNR_proxy)
   184→   Pair selection: time-series subgraph + DEM-sensitivity subgraph
   185→        |
   186→        v
   187→   SLC coregistration (ISCE3 + capella-reader)
   188→   Interferogram formation: I_ij = S_i · S_j*
   189→   Coherence estimation
   190→   Classical baselines: Goldstein, NL-InSAR, BM3D
   191→   Unwrapping: SNAPHU
   192→        |
   193→        v
   194→   DL model: f_θ(I_ij | metadata) → (Î_ij, log σ²)
   195→   Self-supervised training:
   196→     - Noise2Noise (sub-look splits)
   197→     - Heteroscedastic NLL (uncertainty)
   198→     - Closure-consistency triplet loss
   199→     - Temporal-consistency (SBAS residual) loss
   200→     - Spectral/fringe-preservation loss
   201→        |
   202→        v
   203→   Uncertainty-weighted unwrapping (SNAPHU with weights)
   204→   Uncertainty-weighted stack inversion (SBAS)
   205→   DEM generation (where geometry permits)
   206→        |
   207→        v
   208→   Evaluation: closure / unwrap / usable pairs / DEM NMAD / temporal residual
   209→   Visualization: pair graphs, maps, timelines ("temporal storytelling")
   210→   4-page paper + public GitHub
   211→```

   217→```
   218→Week 1 (Mar 05–10): Data access + STAC index + pair-graph skeleton
   219→Week 2 (Mar 10–18): Baseline InSAR products + SNAPHU + closure metrics

   226→
   227→## 6. Phase 1: Data Access and Pair-Graph Construction
   228→
   229→### 6.1 STAC Crawl and Local Index
   230→
   231→**Task 1.1: Crawl contest collection and build metadata parquet**
   232→
   233→```python
   234→# scripts/download_subset.py
   235→import pystac
   236→
   237→root = pystac.Catalog.from_file(
   238→    "https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/catalog.json"
   239→)
   240→contest = pystac.Collection.from_file(
   241→    "https://capella-open-data.s3.us-west-2.amazonaws.com/stac/"
   242→    "capella-open-data-ieee-data-contest/collection.json"
   243→)
   244→
   245→# Traverse items, write each to data/stac_cache/items/<item_id>.json
   246→# Extract to parquet: item_id, datetime, bbox, mode, look_direction,
   247→#   flight_direction, incidence, asset hrefs + sizes
   248→```
   249→
   250→**Task 1.2: Subset selection strategy**
   251→- Inspect mode/incidence/AOI distribution from parquet
   252→- Select 3–6 diverse AOIs covering different land cover and incidence ranges
   253→- Document selection rationale (reproducibility requirement)
   254→- Download manifest with checksums → `data/manifests/subset_manifest.csv`
   255→
   256→### 6.2 Pair-Graph Construction
   257→
   258→**Task 1.3: Node and edge definitions**
   259→
   260→- **Node** v_i: `collect_id, datetime, mode, look_direction, flight_direction, incidence_deg`
   261→- **Edge** e_ij: `Δt, Δθ_inc, Δθ_graze, B_perp (computed from orbits), SNR_proxy`
   262→
   263→**Task 1.4: Perpendicular baseline computation**
   264→
   265→`B_perp` is NOT in the contest CSV — compute from orbit/state vectors using ISCE3:
   266→```python
   267→# src/insar_processing/geometry.py
   268→from isce3.geometry import compute_perpendicular_baseline
   269→```
   270→
   271→**Task 1.5: Edge quality score formula**
   272→
   273→```
   274→Q_ij = 1[mode_compat] × 1[look_compat] × 1[flight_compat]
   275→       × exp(−α_t × Δt/τ_t)
   276→       × exp(−α_inc × |Δθ_inc|/τ_inc)
   277→       × exp(−α_g × |Δθ_graze|/τ_g)
   278→       × exp(−α_b × |B_perp|/τ_b)
   279→       × σ(β₀ + β₁ × SNR_proxy_ij)
   280→```
   281→
   282→Default hyperparameters: `τ_t=30d, τ_inc=5°, τ_g=3°, τ_b=300m`
   283→
   284→**Task 1.6: Pair selection strategy**
   285→
   286→For each AOI, select:
   287→1. **Time-series subgraph**: emphasize small Δt and high Q_ij (for temporal consistency)
   288→2. **DEM-sensitivity subgraph**: emphasize diverse B_perp while keeping Q_ij ≥ threshold
   289→
   290→Cap total edges to compute budget. Document budget in `configs/data/pair_selection.yaml`.
   291→
   292→**Deliverables Phase 1:**
   293→- [ ] `data/stac_cache/` — local STAC item JSONs
   294→- [ ] `data/metadata/stac_index.parquet` — searchable metadata
   295→- [ ] `data/manifests/subset_manifest.csv` — download list with checksums
   296→- [ ] `src/insar_processing/pair_graph.py` — graph construction + scoring
   297→- [ ] `notebooks/01_pair_graph_exploration.ipynb` — visual exploration ("temporal storytelling")
   298→
   299→---
   300→
   301→## 7. Phase 2: Baseline InSAR Products
   302→
   303→### 7.1 SLC Coregistration (ISCE3-first)
   304→
   305→**Task 2.1: Per-pair coregistration**
   306→
   307→```bash
   308→# scripts/preprocess_pairs.py
   309→python scripts/preprocess_pairs.py \
   310→    --manifest data/manifests/subset_manifest.csv \
   311→    --out_dir data/processed/
   312→```
   313→
   314→Steps per pair:
   315→1. Parse metadata with `capella-reader` (orbit, Doppler)
   316→2. Coarse geometric alignment using ISCE3 orbit geometry
   317→3. Refine with correlation offsets
   318→4. Save misregistration metrics (become features for usability predictor)
   319→
   320→### 7.2 Interferogram and Coherence
   321→
   322→**Task 2.2**: Form `I_ij = S_i · conj(S_j)` and estimate coherence in sliding window
   323→
   324→Product outputs per pair (GeoTIFF):
   325→- `interferogram_real.tif`, `interferogram_imag.tif` (or stacked complex)
   326→- `coherence.tif`
   327→- `amplitude_ref.tif`, `amplitude_sec.tif`
   328→
   329→### 7.3 Classical Filtering Baselines
   330→
   331→**Task 2.3**: Implement three non-DL baselines for fair comparison:
   332→1. **Goldstein adaptive filter** — `src/insar_processing/filters.py`
   333→2. **NL-InSAR** (nonlocal estimator) — `src/insar_processing/filters.py`
   334→3. **BM3D-like denoiser** (applied to complex channels) — `src/insar_processing/filters.py`
   335→
   336→### 7.4 Phase Unwrapping
   337→
   338→**Task 2.4: SNAPHU baseline**
   339→
   340→```bash
   341→# scripts/unwrap_snaphu.py
   342→snaphu -f snaphu.conf wrapped_phase.bin <width>
   343→```
   344→
   345→Use consistent coherence mask threshold (report mask percentage). SNAPHU is the required baseline for reproducibility.
   346→
   347→### 7.5 Closure Metrics on Baseline Products
   348→
   349→**Task 2.5**: Compute all 5 contest metrics on classical-baseline products to establish numbers to beat.
   350→
   351→```python
   352→# src/evaluation/closure_metrics.py
   353→def compute_all_contest_metrics(pair_products, triplets, stable_mask, ref_dem=None):
   354→    """Returns dict with all 5 contest metrics for a set of pairs."""
   355→```
   356→
   357→**Deliverables Phase 2:**
   358→- [ ] `data/processed/<aoi>/<pair_id>/` — interferogram, coherence, amplitude, unwrapped phase
   359→- [ ] `src/insar_processing/filters.py` — Goldstein, NL-InSAR, BM3D baselines
   360→- [ ] `scripts/unwrap_snaphu.py` — reproducible unwrapping script
   361→- [ ] `src/evaluation/closure_metrics.py` — all 5 contest metrics
   362→- [ ] Baseline metric numbers documented
   363→
   364→---
   365→
   366→## 8. Phase 3: Deep Learning Method
   367→
   368→### 8.1 Model Architecture
   369→
   370→**Primary choice: U-Net with FiLM metadata conditioning**
   371→
   372→- **Input**: Complex interferogram as 2 channels (Re I_ij, Im I_ij); optionally + coherence channel
   373→- **Conditioning**: FiLM layers conditioned on `[Δt, Δθ_inc, Δθ_graze, B_perp, mode_embed, look_embed, SNR_proxy]`
   374→- **Output**: (1) Denoised complex interferogram Î_ij (2 channels); (2) Per-pixel log-variance `log σ²(p)` (1 channel)
   375→
   376→```python
   377→# src/models/film_unet.py
   378→class FiLMUNet(nn.Module):
   379→    """U-Net with Feature-wise Linear Modulation for geometry conditioning."""
   380→    def __init__(self, in_channels=2, metadata_dim=7, features=[32,64,128,256]):
   381→        ...
   382→    def forward(self, x, metadata):
   383→        # metadata: (B, metadata_dim) tensor
   384→        # returns: denoised (B, 2, H, W), log_var (B, 1, H, W)
   385→```
   386→
   387→**Optional extension (if time permits): Graph-conditioned FiLM** — compute collect-level node embeddings, use edge embedding as FiLM input. Most contest-aligned novel contribution.
   388→
   389→### 8.2 Self-Supervised Training (No Reference DEM Required)
   390→
   391→Training is **fully self-supervised** — the contest provides no ground-truth clean interferograms.
   392→
   393→**Task 3.1: Noise2Noise dataset creation**
   394→
   395→Construct two noisy views (I^(a), I^(b)) per pair using:
   396→- Sub-look / aperture splits from the SLC
   397→- OR stochastic multilook windowing with different random windows
   398→
   399→**Task 3.2: Loss functions**
   400→
   401→```python
   402→# src/losses/physics_losses.py
   403→
   404→# L_N2N: Noise2Noise L1
   405→L_n2n = E[|Î_ij − I^(b)_ij|₁]
   406→
   407→# L_unc: Heteroscedastic NLL (uncertainty)
   408→L_unc = Σ_p [ |Î(p) − I^(b)(p)|² / σ²(p) + log σ²(p) ]
   409→
   410→# L_closure: Closure-consistency triplet loss
   411→c_ijk(p) = wrap(φ̂_ij(p) + φ̂_jk(p) − φ̂_ik(p))
   412→L_closure = Σ_p w(p) × (1 − cos(c_ijk(p)))   # w from uncertainty/coherence
   413→
   414→# L_temporal: Stack inversion residual (SBAS-like)
   415→x* = argmin_x ‖W(Ax − φ̂)‖²
   416→L_temporal = ‖W(Ax* − φ̂)‖²
   417→
   418→# L_grad: Spectral/fringe-preservation
   419→L_grad = ‖∇φ̂ − ∇φ_raw‖₁
   420→
   421→# Combined
   422→L = λ₁L_n2n + λ₂L_unc + λ₃L_closure + λ₄L_temporal + λ₅L_grad
   423→```
   424→
   425→Default: `λ₁=1.0, λ₂=0.5, λ₃=0.3, λ₄=0.2, λ₅=0.1`
   426→
   427→### 8.3 Training Configuration
   428→
   429→**AOI-based splits** (prevents geographic leakage):
   430→- Train AOIs: 60–70%
   431→- Validation AOIs: 10–20%
   432→- Test AOIs: 20–30% (held out until final evaluation)
   433→
   434→**Augmentations** (physically safe):
   435→- 90° rotations, flips
   436→- Global phase offset: `φ → wrap(φ + Δ)` (arbitrary Δ)
   437→- Amplitude scaling in log space
   438→- Random multilook window jitter for Noise2Noise
   439→
   440→**Batch strategy**: sample AOI → sample edge → sample patch. Upsample rare modes and high incidence-difference pairs.
   441→
   442→**Checkpointing**: Save (1) best-by-validation closure error, (2) best-by-validation unwrap success, (3) final epoch. Store `config.yaml`, git hash, dataset manifest per run.
   443→
   444→### 8.4 Uncertainty-Weighted Downstream Integration
   445→
   446→**Task 3.3**: Use predicted `σ²(p)` to weight:
   447→1. SNAPHU inputs: coherence-like weight map from `1/σ²(p)`
   448→2. SBAS stack inversion: design matrix weights `W = diag(1/σ²)`
   449→3. DEM generation: weighted multi-baseline combination
   450→
   451→### 8.5 Training Script
   452→
   453→```bash
   454→python experiments/enhanced/train_film_unet.py \
   455→    --data_config configs/data/capella_aoi_selection.yaml \
   456→    --model_config configs/model/film_unet.yaml \
   457→    --train_config configs/train/contest.yaml
   458→```

1→"""
     2→Classical interferogram filters for phase noise reduction.
     3→
     4→Implementations
     5→---------------
     6→- goldstein()       Goldstein-Werner spectral filter (Goldstein & Werner 1998)
     7→- boxcar()          Multi-look box-car averaging (coherence + phase smoothing)
     8→- adaptive_goldstein()  Coherence-adaptive Goldstein (strength α from coherence)
     9→
    10→All functions operate on complex interferograms (Re + j·Im).
    11→Input / output shapes are always (rows, cols) complex64 or complex128.
    12→"""
    13→
    14→import numpy as np
    15→from scipy.ndimage import uniform_filter
    16→
    17→
    18→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    19→# Goldstein-Werner spectral filter
    20→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    21→
    22→def goldstein(
    23→    ifg: np.ndarray,
    24→    alpha: float = 0.5,
    25→    block_size: int = 32,
    26→    overlap: int = 8,
    27→) -> np.ndarray:
    28→    """
    29→    Goldstein-Werner spectral interferogram filter.
    30→
    31→    Each overlapping block is transformed to the 2-D frequency domain,
    32→    the spectrum is weighted by |S|^alpha, then transformed back.
    33→    Blocks are recombined with cosine-tapered blending.
    34→
    35→    Parameters
    36→    ----------
    37→    ifg : np.ndarray   complex, shape (rows, cols)
    38→    alpha : float      Filter strength in [0, 1].
    39→                       0 = no filtering, 1 = maximum smoothing.
    40→    block_size : int   FFT block size (power of 2 recommended).
    41→    overlap : int      Overlap between adjacent blocks (reduces blocking artefacts).
    42→
    43→    Returns
    44→    -------
    45→    np.ndarray   Filtered complex interferogram, same shape as input.
    46→
    47→    Reference
    48→    ---------
    49→    Goldstein R.M. & Werner C.L. (1998). "Radar interferogram filtering for
    50→    geophysical applications." Geophysical Research Letters 25(21):4035-4038.
    51→    """
    52→    if not np.iscomplexobj(ifg):
    53→        raise TypeError("Input must be complex.")
    54→
    55→    rows, cols = ifg.shape
    56→    step = block_size - overlap
    57→    out = np.zeros_like(ifg, dtype=np.complex128)
    58→    weight = np.zeros((rows, cols), dtype=np.float64)
    59→
    60→    # 2-D cosine taper window for smooth block blending
    61→    taper_1d = np.hanning(block_size)
    62→    taper_2d = np.outer(taper_1d, taper_1d)
    63→
    64→    for r0 in range(0, rows - block_size + 1, step):
    65→        for c0 in range(0, cols - block_size + 1, step):
    66→            block = ifg[r0:r0 + block_size, c0:c0 + block_size].copy()
    67→
    68→            # 2-D FFT
    69→            spec = np.fft.fft2(block)
    70→
    71→            # Smooth spectral magnitude (3×3 uniform filter to avoid noise amplification)
    72→            mag = np.abs(spec)
    73→            mag_smooth = uniform_filter(mag, size=3)
    74→
    75→            # Goldstein weighting: |S|^alpha (normalised to avoid DC gain)
    76→            max_mag = mag_smooth.max()
    77→            if max_mag > 0:
    78→                w = (mag_smooth / max_mag) ** alpha
    79→            else:
    80→                w = np.ones_like(mag_smooth)
    81→
    82→            # Apply filter in frequency domain
    83→            filtered_spec = spec * w
    84→            filtered_block = np.fft.ifft2(filtered_spec)
    85→
    86→            # Accumulate with taper weight
    87→            out[r0:r0 + block_size, c0:c0 + block_size] += filtered_block * taper_2d
    88→            weight[r0:r0 + block_size, c0:c0 + block_size] += taper_2d

    96→def adaptive_goldstein(
    97→    ifg: np.ndarray,
    98→    coherence: np.ndarray,
    99→    alpha_min: float = 0.2,
   100→    alpha_max: float = 0.9,
   101→    block_size: int = 32,
   102→    overlap: int = 8,
   103→) -> np.ndarray:
   104→    """
   105→    Coherence-adaptive Goldstein filter.
   106→
   107→    Filter strength α(p) = alpha_max × (1 − coherence(p)):
   108→    - High coherence → weak filtering (preserve signal fidelity)
   109→    - Low coherence  → strong filtering (suppress noise)
   110→
   111→    Parameters
   112→    ----------
   113→    ifg : np.ndarray        complex, shape (rows, cols)
   114→    coherence : np.ndarray  float [0,1], same shape — per-pixel coherence estimate
   115→    alpha_min : float       minimum α (applied to highest-coherence pixels)
   116→    alpha_max : float       maximum α (applied to lowest-coherence pixels)
   117→    block_size : int
   118→    overlap : int
   119→
   120→    Returns
   121→    -------
   122→    np.ndarray  Filtered complex interferogram.
   123→    """
   124→    rows, cols = ifg.shape
   125→    step = block_size - overlap
   126→    out = np.zeros_like(ifg, dtype=np.complex128)
   127→    weight = np.zeros((rows, cols), dtype=np.float64)

   129→    taper_1d = np.hanning(block_size)

   136→            mean_coh = float(np.nanmean(coh_block))
   137→

   139→            alpha = alpha_min + (alpha_max - alpha_min) * (1.0 - mean_coh)
   140→            alpha = float(np.clip(alpha, alpha_min, alpha_max))

   148→            filtered_block = np.fft.ifft2(spec * w)

   157→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   158→# Multi-look (box-car) coherence + phase
   159→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   160→
   161→def boxcar_coherence(
   162→    ifg: np.ndarray,
   163→    slc_ref: np.ndarray,
   164→    slc_sec: np.ndarray,
   165→    looks_range: int = 5,
   166→    looks_azimuth: int = 5,
   167→) -> np.ndarray:
   168→    """
   169→    Estimate interferometric coherence via multi-look box-car averaging.
   170→
   171→        γ = |<slc_ref × conj(slc_sec)>| / sqrt(<|slc_ref|²> × <|slc_sec|²>)
   172→
   173→    Parameters
   174→    ----------
   175→    ifg : np.ndarray   complex ifg = slc_ref × conj(slc_sec), shape (rows, cols)
   176→    slc_ref, slc_sec : np.ndarray   complex SLCs, same shape
   177→    looks_range : int   number of looks in range (columns)
   178→    looks_azimuth : int number of looks in azimuth (rows)
   179→
   180→    Returns
   181→    -------
   182→    np.ndarray float32 [0, 1], same shape — per-pixel coherence estimate.
   183→    """
   184→    ksize = (looks_azimuth, looks_range)
   185→
   186→    # Multi-look numerator: |mean of ifg over window|
   187→    re_avg = uniform_filter(ifg.real.astype(np.float64), size=ksize)
   188→    im_avg = uniform_filter(ifg.imag.astype(np.float64), size=ksize)
   189→    numerator = np.sqrt(re_avg ** 2 + im_avg ** 2)
   190→
   191→    # Multi-look denominator: sqrt(mean(|ref|²) × mean(|sec|²))
   192→    ref_pwr = uniform_filter(np.abs(slc_ref).astype(np.float64) ** 2, size=ksize)
   193→    sec_pwr = uniform_filter(np.abs(slc_sec).astype(np.float64) ** 2, size=ksize)
   194→    denominator = np.sqrt(ref_pwr * sec_pwr + 1e-30)
   195→
   196→    coherence = np.clip(numerator / denominator, 0.0, 1.0)
   197→    return coherence.astype(np.float32)

   199→
   200→def multilook(
   201→    arr: np.ndarray,
   202→    looks_range: int = 5,
   203→    looks_azimuth: int = 5,
   204→) -> np.ndarray:
   205→    """
   206→    Multi-look (box-car average) a real or complex array.
   207→    Output is the same shape as input (full-resolution, windowed average).
   208→    """
   209→    ksize = (looks_azimuth, looks_range)
   210→    if np.iscomplexobj(arr):
   211→        re = uniform_filter(arr.real.astype(np.float64), size=ksize)
   212→        im = uniform_filter(arr.imag.astype(np.float64), size=ksize)
   213→        return (re + 1j * im).astype(arr.dtype)
   214→    return uniform_filter(arr.astype(np.float64), size=ksize).astype(arr.dtype)

    27→# Core sub-look splitting
    28→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
    29→
    30→def split_sublooks_fft(
    31→    slc: np.ndarray,
    32→    axis: int = 1,
    33→    n_looks: int = 2,
    34→    overlap: float = 0.0,
    35→) -> list[np.ndarray]:
    36→    """
    37→    Split a complex SLC into n_looks independent sub-looks via FFT sub-banding.
    38→
    39→    Each sub-look spans 1/n_looks of the full bandwidth along the chosen axis.
    40→    Sub-looks have independent speckle realisations, making them suitable as
    41→    Noise2Noise training pairs.
    42→
    43→    Parameters
    44→    ----------
    45→    slc : np.ndarray complex64 or complex128, shape (rows, cols)
    46→        Input complex SAR SLC in image (pixel) domain.
    47→    axis : int
    48→        Frequency axis to split: 0 = azimuth, 1 = range.
    49→    n_looks : int
    50→        Number of sub-looks (typically 2 for N2N pairs).
    51→    overlap : float
    52→        Fractional overlap between adjacent sub-bands [0, 0.5).
    53→        0.0 = no overlap (independent speckle); small values reduce resolution loss.
    54→
    55→    Returns
    56→    -------
    57→    list[np.ndarray]
    58→        n_looks complex arrays each of the same shape as slc.
    59→        Each sub-look is back-projected to the full image grid (upsampled
    60→        from sub-band) so they are spatially registered with each other.
    61→    """
    62→    if slc.ndim != 2:
    63→        raise ValueError(f"Expected 2-D array, got shape {slc.shape}")
    64→    if not np.iscomplexobj(slc):
    65→        raise ValueError("Input must be complex (complex SLC).")
    66→
    67→    n = slc.shape[axis]
    68→
    69→    # Transform to frequency domain along chosen axis
    70→    spec = np.fft.fft(slc, axis=axis)
    71→    spec = np.fft.fftshift(spec, axes=axis)  # centre DC
    72→
    73→    band_width = int(n / n_looks * (1.0 + overlap))
    74→    band_width = min(band_width, n)
    75→
    76→    sublooks = []
    77→    for k in range(n_looks):
    78→        centre = int(n / n_looks * (k + 0.5))  # band centre index
    79→        half = band_width // 2
    80→        lo = max(centre - half, 0)
    81→        hi = min(centre + half, n)

    91→        sub_spec = np.fft.ifftshift(sub_spec, axes=axis)
    92→        sub_img = np.fft.ifft(sub_spec, axis=axis)
    93→        # Scale to preserve amplitude statistics
    94→        sub_img = sub_img * (n / band_width) ** 0.5
    95→        sublooks.append(sub_img.astype(slc.dtype))

   103→

   106→    Each output has half the rows (axis=0) or columns (axis=1) of the input.
   107→
   108→    Parameters
   109→    ----------
   110→    slc : np.ndarray   complex, shape (rows, cols)
   111→    axis : int         0 = split azimuth (rows), 1 = split range (cols)

   116→    """

   122→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   123→# Interferogram N2N pair generation
   124→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   125→
   126→def make_n2n_pair(
   127→    slc_ref: np.ndarray,
   128→    slc_sec: np.ndarray,
   129→    axis: int = 1,
   130→    method: str = "fft",
   131→) -> tuple[np.ndarray, np.ndarray]:
   132→    """
   133→    Generate a Noise2Noise training pair from two registered complex SLCs.
   134→
   135→    Strategy
   136→    --------
   137→    1. Split both SLCs into sub-looks 1 and 2.
   138→    2. Form interferogram_A = sub_ref_1 × conj(sub_sec_1)
   139→       Form interferogram_B = sub_ref_2 × conj(sub_sec_2)
   140→    3. Return (ifg_A, ifg_B) — same scene, independent speckle.
   141→
   142→    A model trained with input=ifg_A, target=ifg_B learns to denoise
   143→    without ever seeing a clean reference interferogram.
   144→
   145→    Parameters
   146→    ----------
   147→    slc_ref, slc_sec : np.ndarray   complex, registered SLC pair, same shape
   148→    axis : int   frequency axis for sub-look splitting (1 = range, typically)
   149→    method : str  "fft" (spectral sub-banding) or "odd_even" (line interleaving)
   150→
   151→    Returns
   152→    -------
   153→    ifg_a, ifg_b : np.ndarray complex  N2N input/target interferogram pair
   154→    """
   155→    if slc_ref.shape != slc_sec.shape:
   156→        raise ValueError(
   157→            f"SLCs must have matching shapes: {slc_ref.shape} vs {slc_sec.shape}"
   158→        )
   159→
   160→    if method == "fft":
   161→        ref_subs = split_sublooks_fft(slc_ref, axis=axis, n_looks=2)
   162→        sec_subs = split_sublooks_fft(slc_sec, axis=axis, n_looks=2)
   163→    elif method == "odd_even":
   164→        ref_subs = list(split_sublooks_odd_even(slc_ref, axis=axis))
   165→        sec_subs = list(split_sublooks_odd_even(slc_sec, axis=axis))
   166→    else:
   167→        raise ValueError(f"Unknown method: {method!r}. Use 'fft' or 'odd_even'.")
   168→
   169→    ifg_a = ref_subs[0] * np.conj(sec_subs[0])
   170→    ifg_b = ref_subs[1] * np.conj(sec_subs[1])
   171→    return ifg_a, ifg_b
   172→
   173→
   174→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   175→# Tile extraction for training
   176→# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   177→
   178→def extract_sublook_tiles(
   179→    slc_ref: np.ndarray,
   180→    slc_sec: np.ndarray,
   181→    tile_size: int = 256,
   182→    stride: int = 128,
   183→    axis: int = 1,
   184→    method: str = "fft",
   185→    min_coherence: float = 0.2,
   186→) -> list[dict]:
   187→    """
   188→    Slide a window over the SLC pair and return N2N tile dicts.
   189→
   190→    Each tile dict contains:
   191→        "ifg_a"   : np.ndarray complex64 (tile_size, tile_size)  — N2N input
   192→        "ifg_b"   : np.ndarray complex64 (tile_size, tile_size)  — N2N target
   193→        "row_off" : int   top-left row offset in original image
   194→        "col_off" : int   top-left col offset in original image
   195→
   196→    Tiles with mean coherence below min_coherence are skipped (incoherent regions
   197→    provide no training signal for interferogram denoising).
   198→
   199→    Parameters
   200→    ----------
   201→    slc_ref, slc_sec : np.ndarray complex, registered SLCs
   202→    tile_size : int   spatial tile size (same in both dims)
   203→    stride : int      stride between tiles (< tile_size for overlap)
   204→    axis : int        sub-look split axis
   205→    method : str      "fft" or "odd_even"
   206→    min_coherence : float   minimum mean coherence to include a tile
   207→    """
   208→    rows, cols = slc_ref.shape
   209→    tiles = []
   210→
   211→    for r in range(0, rows - tile_size + 1, stride):
   212→        for c in range(0, cols - tile_size + 1, stride):
   213→            ref_tile = slc_ref[r:r + tile_size, c:c + tile_size]
   214→            sec_tile = slc_sec[r:r + tile_size, c:c + tile_size]
   215→
   216→            ifg_a, ifg_b = make_n2n_pair(ref_tile, sec_tile, axis=axis, method=method)
   217→
   218→            # Quick coherence proxy: magnitude of normalised mean ifg
   219→            full_ifg = ref_tile * np.conj(sec_tile)
   220→            coh_proxy = float(
   221→                np.abs(np.mean(full_ifg))
   222→                / (np.mean(np.abs(ref_tile)) * np.mean(np.abs(sec_tile)) + 1e-10)
   223→            )
   224→            if coh_proxy < min_coherence:
   225→                continue
   226→
   227→            tiles.append({
   228→                "ifg_a": ifg_a.astype(np.complex64),
   229→                "ifg_b": ifg_b.astype(np.complex64),
   230→                "coherence_proxy": coh_proxy,
   231→                "row_off": r,
   232→                "col_off": c,
   233→            })
   234→
   235→    return tiles
   236→
